title: Campaign Claims: What the Numbers Measure Matters
summary:
A campaign speech can contain a striking number without explaining everything behind it. That is the puzzle in a PolitiFact review, republished by PBS NewsHour, of President Donald Trump's statements before the midterm elections.

Trump is supporting Republican candidates in competitive races. The results will determine which party controls Congress during the last two years of his presidency. PolitiFact examined remarks from speeches and interviews, checking claims against available records.

Consider investment. Trump said $22 trillion was coming into the United States from abroad. PolitiFact found $11.2 trillion listed on the White House website. It also cautioned that the website's total included ambitious plans extending across several years. Some entries concerned future product purchases or sales, rather than capital investment: money put into projects or businesses. A pledge is therefore different from a completed investment.

Retirement savings provide another example. Trump said Americans' 401(k) accounts had risen by about $46,000. These are retirement savings accounts. Fidelity Investments data showed an average increase of $9,454 between December 31, 2024, and March 31, 2026. PolitiFact said the much larger claim was unsupported. An average, however, is not a statement about every person's account.

One employment claim had a factual basis but needed context. More than 159 million people were employed in August, a record partly explained by population growth. The labor force participation rate and the share of people aged 25 to 54 who are employed were not at record highs.

Prices were mixed, too. Through August, overall prices had increased about 4.7 percent since Trump's second term began, and grocery prices about 3.4 percent. Coffee, ground beef and chicken breast were more expensive, while eggs, bacon and bread were cheaper.

The review also examined tax claims. It said some breaks for tipped workers, overtime earners and older Americans expire in 2028 unless Congress extends them.

The lesson in reading these claims is specific: check the measurement, the dates and the qualifications. A record total, a future promise and a change in an average describe different things.
why_it_matters: The same number can be understood differently when its dates, measurement and limits are missing.

questions.question: What is the difference between an investment pledge and a completed investment?
options: A pledge concerns savings; completion means money withdrawn
A pledge concerns wages; completion means money earned
A pledge concerns taxes; completion means money collected
A pledge concerns plans; completion means money invested
questions.correct_answer: A pledge concerns plans; completion means money invested

options: They fell $46,000 over the stated period
They rose $9,454 over the stated period
They fell $9,454 over the stated period
They rose $46,000 over the stated period
questions.correct_answer: They rose $9,454 over the stated period
